title: Rockstar Parent Company Takes Down Leaked GTA 5 DLC and GTA 6 Map Content
description: Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has started removing videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content across the web.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Take-Two and Rockstar Crack Down on Leaked Content

For fans eagerly following the development of Grand Theft Auto VI, any piece of unofficial information often becomes the center of community discussion. However, the availability of these unauthorized previews is changing as copyright holders step up their enforcement. According to a recent report by IGN, Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts featuring leaked content from both Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto VI.

## Targeting Scrapped DLCs and Early Map Footage

The enforcement efforts are reportedly focusing on specific categories of leaked material that have circulated online over time:

* **Scrapped GTA 5 DLC Material:** Footage and images related to single-player downloadable content projects that were ultimately abandoned by the developer.
* **Early GTA 6 Map Leaks:** Visuals and media originating from earlier development builds, specifically involving early versions of the leaked map for GTA 6.

For years, these unreleased assets have been heavily discussed by data miners and enthusiasts alike. While such leaks often generate significant online chatter, publishers frequently argue that unfinished or scrapped work does not reflect the final product's quality and infringes on proprietary assets. This latest wave of takedowns highlights Take-Two's active stance on managing its intellectual property and development secrets.

## Context and Industry Standard

In the gaming industry, publishers routinely issue takedown notices under copyright laws when internal or unreleased materials are shared publicly without authorization. Observers note that as development continues, tightening control over early assets is a typical measure to protect the integrity of a studio's future marketing pipeline and final releases.

## Editor's Take

Take-Two's decision to remove leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content is a standard copyright enforcement move. While it limits early and often misleading looks at unreleased projects, it ultimately paves the way for controlled, official reveals when the time is right.
